title: Parent with only parameterized constructors
answer: If a superclass has no accessible no-argument constructor, a subclass constructor must explicitly invoke one of the available superclass constructors with matching arguments. Otherwise the compiler tries to insert `super()` and compilation fails because no such constructor exists. AeroTopo's `Product` declares parameterized constructors and `Orthomosaic` explicitly calls `super(id, tiles)`, so inherited Product state can be initialized correctly.
